application.name: ofetch
application.summary: A TypeScript HTTP client built on Fetch that simplifies request configuration, response parsing, retries, hooks, and error handling.
application.purpose: Provide a convenient, typed API for making HTTP requests across browser and Node.js environments.

domains.name: HTTP request execution
domains.description: Builds and sends requests with URL, query, body, header, timeout, and abort options.

domains.name: Response handling
domains.description: Parses response bodies according to explicit options or the response Content-Type.

domains.name: Errors and retries
domains.description: Retries selected failures and exposes request, response, and status details in normalized errors.

domains.name: Configuration and hooks
domains.description: Supports shared defaults, customized client instances, and lifecycle hooks.

domains.name: Runtime support
domains.description: Provides Fetch implementations and related primitives for global and Node.js environments.

applicationFacts: The client exposes $fetch/ofetch for parsed response data, $fetch.raw for the Fetch response with parsed data attached, and $fetch.native for the underlying fetch function.
Request options support base URLs, query and parameter values, headers, JSON body serialization, timeouts, abort signals, retries, and lifecycle hooks.
When no response type is specified, the client selects JSON, text, or blob parsing based on the response Content-Type; callers can also choose a response type or custom parser.
Retries can be disabled, set to a number, delayed by a number or callback, and limited to selected status codes.
The Node.js entry point uses global fetch when available and otherwise falls back to node-fetch-native; keep-alive can be enabled with FETCH_KEEP_ALIVE.
The type-safety example demonstrates that callers can specify a response type for the returned data.
